A_open.text: Saturday. Six a.m. The sun has not yet decided to participate.
Is the sun supposed to be this late?
Sun starts when the pumpkins do.
Uncle Gord. About last night. About Patch Seven...
Three jobs. Water. Plant. Haul. Do them right.
Walk to each job and press Action: the trough, the seed row, and the cart.

do.text: A row of tiny wooden markers by the fence. WALTER: Grew big. Became pie. MARVIN: Stepped on by goose.
You keep a pumpkin graveyard.
They deserve it.
Of course they do.

job_water.text: A pumpkin drinks when it's thirsty. Not when it's convenient.
Brad hauls the watering can down the row. Most of it goes on his boots.
Doris leans toward the water as if she were listening.
There, there, Doris. Brad's new. Be kind.
He talks to Doris more tenderly than he's ever talked to me.

job_plant.text: Gord hands Brad a seed the size of a thumbnail.
To... grow up? Big? And not die in the first week?

job_haul.text: Lift with your knees. Think with your gut.
Brad lifts a pumpkin the size of an armchair. He lifts it three inches. It lifts him back.
The pumpkin hums. A low, rumbling purr that travels through Brad's chest.
It's humming! Uncle Gord, it's humming at me!

B_patch.text: Lunch is pumpkin sandwiches. Gord eats in silence. Then he stands.
Need to check the shed. Stay in the yard.
Sure thing.
The moment Gord disappears, a low hum rolls across the yard. It seems to come from the back field.
Patch Seven. The pumpkins are the size of armchairs. They were not this big on Thursday.
Their skins glow a faint orange in the late light. The hum is as low as a refrigerator the size of a barn.
Three feet in two days. What are you feeding them?
The pumpkins hum back, as if answering.
Brad kneels and scoops a handful of soil. Orange flecks sparkle between his fingers, like glitter.
The same orange. The same as the foam in the lab.
Wash your hands. Now.
Gord stands at the fence line, a silhouette against the golden light. His hands are shaking.
I said stay in the yard. Don't go near Patch Seven.
It's the soil. It's the same as in the lab. Professor Peters's sample reacted with it.
...Your father's boots. Of course.
Gord pulls a grease pencil and a loose plank from the fence. He writes: KEEP OUT. PATCH 7.
In the corner, out of habit, he doodles a tiny pumpkin.
That doodle.
Brad pulls out the folded note. Same block capitals. Same curl on the R. Same tiny pumpkin.
You wrote this. You put it in my jacket.
...Aye.
I made a promise to your father. A long time ago. I'm not good at breaking promises.

B_patch.prompt: Gord looks at the ground. He is ashamed, and scared.

do.text: What promise? What dance? Tell me. Now.
Boy. You don't know what you're asking.
...Fine. The patch blooms on a full moon. Halloween's a full moon this year. That's all you get.
Don't ask for more. Please.
Okay. I'll wait. But I'm not going to stop wondering.
Fair. After Halloween. Thank you, boy.
For the first time since Brad arrived, Gord looks like he can breathe.

B_patch.text: Gord nails the plank to the fence post. The pumpkins hum louder, as if they disagree.
Later that afternoon, a visitor arrives at the farm.

C_j.text: Dusk. Jane waits on a hay bale just outside the new fence, two thermoses in her lap.
Dad's in the shed. Sit. We're not going in. We're watching.
The patch pulses with soft orange light. It looks like a very large, very slow heartbeat.
I come here sometimes. Don't tell Dad. It's the only place the world gets quiet.
It does that when it likes someone.
I want to leave sometimes. See an ocean. I've never seen one. Only the pond.
I've seen an ocean. It's like a pond but angrier.
That's the best description I've ever heard.
Dad would be lost without me. Or he'd say he wouldn't. Same thing, with Dad.
The patch brightens. The hum deepens. The pumpkins seem to lean toward them.

C_j.prompt: Something in the field is waking up.

do.text: We should tell your dad. He shouldn't face this alone.
He'll shut down.
...Saw you two out here. Good. Someone ought to watch it besides me.
Dad?

options.text: Walk to the fence with Jane

do.text: Let's go closer. Just to the fence.
They stand at the fence. Jane lays a hand on the nearest pumpkin. It's warm.
Like a heartbeat. Brad, it knows I'm here.
Jane's other hand finds Brad's. Neither of them mentions it.
I'll keep this between us. Until you tell me otherwise.
Pinkie promise?
Brad links pinkies with Jane. Her grip is warm and a little rough, like someone who works for a living.

C_s.text: A battered truck marked LOG & STUMP backs into the yard. Sandra climbs out, scowling.
Kegs. Pumpkin ale. Where do you want them?
A very large goose comes flapping out of the barn. It is not friendly.
The Admiral. We have a history.
Since I was twelve. He hates black clothing. I hate him.

do.text: Hey! Admiral! Over here!
Brad waves a pumpkin. The goose pivots. Sandra unloads a keg while Brad leads the Admiral in circles.
That was the bravest thing anyone's done for me. It involved a goose.
Take this!
Sandra brandishes the shovel. The goose backs off, muttering.
A fair weapon. Thanks.
Brad steps back. The Admiral chases Sandra twice around the truck.
A little help would have been nice.
I wasn't sure which of you I'd be helping.

C_s.text: Afterwards, Sandra scoops a jar of soil from the yard. She does it with the care of a pastry chef.
For science. And for the ledger.
She pulls an old tavern ledger from the truck. A yellowed page is marked with a paper clip.
My grandfather's. Twenty-five years ago. Read it.
In faded ink: College Halloween dance. Punch ingredients: pumpkin. CANCELLED. NEVER AGAIN.
Brad shows her the note from his pocket. Sandra studies the block capitals.
Someone has a theatrical streak. Very serial killer.
I'll compare the soil to the ledger. You keep asking questions.

C_g.text: Georgia arrives with a wheelbarrow, pie crates, and a notebook labeled PUMPKIN SPICE INDEX.
Brad! I'm picking up pumpkins! Gord said I could have the best ones!
She hugs a large pumpkin near the fence. It hums.
This is Bartholomew. He hums. Listen.
Georgia. Are these Patch Seven pumpkins?
I've used only the back patch since June. They taste like... more.

then.text: Please don't mail my application yet. I'm still working up to it.

C_g.text: And I got asked to make the punch for the Halloween dance! Two hundred cups!
Punch. For the dance. With Patch Seven pumpkins.

C_g.prompt: Georgia is so happy. Brad knows what the pumpkins do.

do.text: Georgia, those pumpkins are strange. The soil glows. Gord put up a sign. And you've seen what they do.
...Oh. The thirty minutes.
I could dilute them. Mix in regular pumpkins. Thank you for telling me.
That's wonderful. Two hundred cups. Congratulations.
Thank you! You're the first to say congratulations!
Brad feels a pang of guilt. She loads twelve more Patch Seven pumpkins into the wheelbarrow.

C_p.text: A figure creeps along the fence line. Trench coat. Sunglasses. Binoculars. Sensible shoes.
Mr. Bart! I'm birdwatching. Ravens. The migratory kind.
She kneels by the fence and scoops soil into a thermos, with the air of a spy collecting a state secret.
Retired. She doesn't answer questions about pumpkins.
I was sorry. About the lab. About all of it.
You always were. It never fixed anything.
Neither of them looks at the other. Brad realizes they have a history longer than the fence.

C_p.prompt: Patricia is trespassing. Gord is watching.

do.text: She's with me. It's a school project. Ecology. Ravens, soil, the usual.
...Ecology. Fine. Take what you need.
Thank you, Mr. Bart. That was convincing. Barely.
Professor. Why are you taking soil from Gord's field?
To prevent a disaster. That's all I'll say.
Then say it plainly, Patricia. You've never been good at that.
The air between them goes cold. Brad wishes he'd said nothing.

options.text: Tell Gord about the lab accident

then.text: The sample reacted with my boots. I told Professor Peters. She didn't blame me.
He told me first. That mattered.

else.text: There was an accident in the lab. The sample reacted with soil from your farm.
You didn't confess it to me. You told him instead.

C_p.text: I have what I need. Mr. Bart, Gordon. Good afternoon.
She leaves with her thermos, her binoculars, and her dignity. The dignity is slightly muddy.

D_close.text: Night. The farmhouse kitchen. Gord sets down two mugs of pumpkin cocoa. His hands are steadier now.
Your father hated pumpkins. Did you know?
He... what? He made me pumpkin pie every Thanksgiving.
He ate it with a look of betrayal. Every year. He loved you more.
That might be the nicest thing you've said to me.
Brad. Give me until Halloween. Then I'll tell you everything.
Your father and I made a promise. Let me find the way to break it.

D_close.prompt: Gord is asking, not ordering. It is hard for him.

do.text: Okay. Until Halloween. I promise.
Thank you, boy. Your father would be proud.
I can't promise. Not when people could get hurt.
...I'd have refused too. At your age.
Just be careful. Please.

D_close.text: Pumpkins don't wait. Neither does Monday.
On the chimney, the crow sits with a name tag in its beak. It looks, for once, almost sympathetic.
